title: Building an eCQM: Populations and Exclusions
description: Put it all together: build a real measure with Initial Population (diabetes + age window), Denominator (office visit), Denominator Exclusion (hospice), and Numerator (recent HbA1c) — the exact shape of CMS quality measures.
learningObjectives: Build Initial Population from condition + age criteria
Gate the Denominator on encounters during the period
Read per-patient population membership across a 5-patient cohort

hints.message: define "Measurement Period": Interval[@2024-01-01, @2024-12-31] — a named interval you can reuse everywhere.
exists([Condition] C where exists(C.code.coding cod where cod.code = '44054006' and cod.system = 'http://snomed.info/sct')) — SNOMED diabetes code with system match.
AgeInYearsAt(start of "Measurement Period") — measures age at the period start (2024-01-01).
"Has Diabetes" and "Age At Start" between 18 and 75 — reference earlier defines by name; between is inclusive.
exists([Encounter] E where E.class.code = 'AMB' and E.period during "Measurement Period") — the whole encounter must fall inside the period.
Hospice care shows as Encounter class 'HH' (home health/hospice) — same during test as office visits.
"Initial Population" and "Had Office Visit" — populations build on each other with and.
"Denominator" and "In Hospice" — exclusions only apply INSIDE the denominator.
LOINC 4548-4 (Hemoglobin A1c), effective during the period — remember the choice-type cast: (O.effective as FHIR.dateTime) during "Measurement Period".
"Denominator" and not "Denominator Exclusion" and "Has Recent A1c" — exclude first, then require the metric. Bob has an A1c but is hospice-excluded!
